# Baccarat — what it does, in plain language

Baccarat is one contract on Kadena Community Edition (kda-chain.org) that deals Punto Banco
from a shoe of 8 decks. A round opens the moment somebody places the first bet, takes
bets for a fixed window, and is then dealt from a random number produced by a group of
independent organisations **outside Kadena entirely**. Nobody deals: the players open the round,
anybody settles it, and the winners collect.

> **Two different people appear on this page, and the difference matters.**
>
> - **The house** is whoever holds the signing key. It puts capital into the pot, sets the
>   table's limits, and takes the pot's earnings out. It never plays, it sends no transaction
>   inside a round, and it holds no secret of any kind.
> - **A player** is anyone who places a bet. A player needs no permission from the house, and —
>   like anyone at all — can settle a round, keep the refund clock from running, or send a
>   winner's collection for them.
>
> **So "you" on this page always means a player.** The house is never "you"; it is always named.

> 🔴 **Until the contract is locked, the house's key can take the pot — and replace the rules.**
>
> Everything below describes the contract's own rules, and that one key is the exception to all
> of them: it can move the pot, and it can replace the code, including how a round still waiting
> for its cards is decided. *What the house can and cannot do* says exactly what it can do
> instead. The contract is not locked today, and locking it ends this for good.

## In one minute

**What it can do**

- ✅ Pay Player, Banker and Tie at the official odds, and return a Player or Banker bet when the hands tie.
- ✅ Take every card from a beacon produced away from Kadena, and check its proof on chain.
- ✅ Lock each round to a beacon that does not exist yet, and stop taking bets a fixed wait before it appears.
- ✅ Let anyone settle a round, and pay a winner's money to the winner whoever sends the transaction.
- ✅ Reserve the worst outcome before accepting a bet, so the pot can never fail to pay one it took.
- ✅ Keep a real shoe: cards leave the pool as they are dealt, and the pool is refilled at the cut card.
- ✅ Refund a round rather than keep it, if the beacon is ever retired.

**What it cannot do**

- ✅ **Choose or steer a card** — the house included. Every card is worked out from a beacon nobody
  here produces, and the proof is checked by the contract itself.
- ✅ **Change a round once it has opened.** Its closing time, its beacon, its share of the pot, its
  minimum, its commission, its cut and what the pot owes on every outcome are all fixed by its
  first bet; the table limit is measured against the smaller of the pot at open and the pot now,
  so it can only get smaller while the round is open.
- ✅ **Take the fee out of your stake.** The fee comes out of the pot, and it only decides how much
  of the pot's own earnings are forwarded rather than kept.
- ✅ **Pause a round, cancel it, or reverse a bet.** There is no pause button, no override and no
  undo: a live round keeps the limits it opened with, it is refunded only after ninety days with
  no later beacon on record, and nothing is paid out before the cards are dealt — a wrong bet stays wrong,
  and so does a winning one. Stopping *future* rounds is a different thing, and the house can
  (see "What the house can and cannot do", below).
- ✅ **Reshuffle the shoe by hand, or deal coups out of order.** The shoe is refilled by the
  contract at the cut card and by nothing else, and round two is never dealt before round one.
- ✅ **Stop a winner collecting.** Collecting needs nobody's permission and nobody's cooperation.
- ✅ **Recover a lost key.** A lost key is lost: on Kadena an account *is* its key, and winnings can
  only ever be paid to the account that placed the bet — nobody, the house included, can point
  them anywhere else.
- ✅ **Stop the house's key from taking the pot, until the contract is locked.** That is the one
  exception to everything above, and locking the contract is what ends it.

## The money

| Bet | Pays | Your return | The house's edge |
|---|---|---|---|
| **Player** | 1 to 1, and returned on a tie | 98.765% | 1.2351% |
| **Banker** | 0.95 to 1 — a 5% commission on the win — and returned on a tie | 98.942% | 1.0579% |
| **Tie** | 8 to 1 | 85.640% | 14.3596% |

✅ Those figures are the exact odds of 8 decks: the Player hand wins 44.6247% of coups, the Banker hand 45.8597%, and they tie 9.5156%.
✅ The contract holds the odds as that arithmetic, and the fee and the edge follow from it rather than from typed numbers.
✅ The Banker commission is a house setting, and the contract refuses any commission below 2.6932%, the point at which the Banker bet would pay out more than the pot expects to win.
✅ The commission you accept is part of the board you sign: a board is refused, never paid at a worse rate, if the round's commission is above it.
✅ What Player and Tie pay is fixed, and no house setting reaches it.

✅ The fee is taken from the pot, never from a stake, at each bet's own edge and never more.
✅ The fee is smaller while the pot is below its target, and reaches each bet's edge only once the pot is healthy, so a thin pot keeps more of its own earnings and refills.

| Money | Who gets it | When |
|---|---|---|
| **A losing stake** | The pot | The moment the round settles — nobody sends anything |
| **A winning board** | The player who placed it, at the official odds for every bet that won, with tied Player and Banker stakes returned | When the player, or anyone at all on their behalf, sends the collection |
| **The fee** | The account the house names at the start | Inside the settling transaction |
| **A refunded round** | Every player, their whole stake back. No fee is taken | When the player, or anyone at all, sends the collection |

✅ The pot reserves the worst of the three outcomes for the whole round before it accepts a bet. It can refuse a bet; it can never run short on one it took.
✅ Every payout is rounded to the coin's own precision where it is reserved and again where it is paid, so a fully collected round leaves nothing locked and nothing over.
✅ What the pot has reserved never exceeds what the pot holds, at any point in a round's life.
✅ A loser never sends anything: the pot releases what it reserved the moment the round settles.

**The table limit.**
✅ A round can never put more than the share of the pot's spare capital the house has set.
✅ That share is 2% today.
✅ The house can change it at any time, including after the contract is locked.
✅ The contract's own bound on it is arithmetic and nothing else: a share above 100% of the spare capital is refused, because a round cannot risk more than the pot has spare.
🟡 The share the contract starts with is below the level at which the bank would stop growing, for every one of the three bets.
🟡 Above roughly 4.8% the bank stops growing on Banker bets at today's commission: that is advice the house followed in choosing today's share, not a limit the contract puts on the house.
🟡 Lowering the commission lowers that ceiling too, and at 3% it would fall under today's share: the house's own capital, and the house's own choice.
✅ The limit is measured against the smaller of the pot when the round opened and the pot now.
✅ Money put into the pot mid-round cannot widen a table beyond what it opened with.
✅ The limit bounds the whole round rather than one player, so a round can fill up and a bet is then refused until the next one.
🟡 The play page shows two maxima for each bet: the largest the round accepts now, and one 250th of the spare pot, which is what the pot is sized to keep through a year of play.

**The earnings account.**
✅ Where the house's earnings go is fixed once at the start and can never be named again.
✅ Taking money out of the pot can only pay that one account, never one chosen at the time.
✅ Money already reserved against open rounds cannot be taken out.

## The shoe

✅ The shoe is a pool of 416 cards — 8 decks of 52 kinds — and the contract keeps a count of each kind still in it.
✅ Each card of a coup is picked from what remains by the coup's own beacon, so no card exists until that beacon does, and anyone can recompute the coup once it has.
✅ Cards leave the pool as they are dealt, and the cards a coup did not need go back.
✅ When 52 cards or fewer remain the pool is refilled before the next coup is dealt.
✅ The cut is a house setting: the contract refuses a cut under 14 cards or over a full shoe, and a round keeps the cut it opened under.
✅ At a full-shoe cut every coup is dealt from a fresh shoe.
✅ Coups are dealt in round order: a later round is refused until the earlier one is settled, so the pool a coup draws from never depends on who settled first.
✅ A stalled round that is refunded takes its turn in that order without dealing.

**What a public shoe means.** 🟡 The cards left in the pool are public, so anyone can compute the
exact odds of the next coup from them, and the play page shows those odds to everyone. 🟡 Very
rarely a bet is better than even for the player for one coup. 🟡 Measured over 2,000 shoes, a
perfect card counter betting the table's cap at every such moment would gain about 0.002 KDA per
shoe at a one-deck cut, about 0.65 at the floor of 14 cards, and nothing when the cut is two decks
or more. 🟡 That floor is the deepest cut a gaming regulation asks for, so such a rule can be met
without changing the contract.

---

## A round, step by step

1. **You place a board.**
   ✅ You sign one transaction and nothing else.
   ✅ Your whole board — any mix of Player, Banker and Tie — goes in that one transaction, and a second board in the same round is refused.
   ✅ The first bet of a round opens it, and fixes the closing time, the beacon, the limit, the minimum, the commission and the cut for everyone who joins it.
2. **The round takes bets.**
   ✅ A round takes bets for 2 minutes, by the chain's own clock, and not a moment longer.
   ✅ The beacon the round is locked to appears a fixed wait after betting closes, so it does not exist while a bet can still be placed.
   🟡 The contract starts with that wait at 2 minutes; the house's current setting is shown on the play page, read from the chain.
   ✅ The wait before the beacon is the house's setting, and the contract refuses anything under 60 seconds or over 1 hour.
   🟡 That floor is the lowest the setting can go and not a value that is safe to run at — the house runs well above it — because at 60 seconds roughly one round in fourteen would have no block between its close and its beacon, and a watcher could then read the beacon and bet on it, out of the pot and never out of another player's stake.
   ✅ A round that has opened keeps the beacon it was given, whatever the house does to the wait afterwards.
   ✅ The next round to open takes the new wait.
   🟡 If the chain stopped producing blocks for longer than the wait, one round would be exposed: the one open when it stopped, and only up to that round's own limit.
   ✅ The round's beacon is chosen at the moment the round opens, long before anyone can know what it says.
3. **The beacon is published, and the cards fall out of it.**
   The beacon comes from a group of independent organisations that publish a new random value
   every 3 seconds, on their own network, with nothing to do with Kadena.
   ✅ Anyone at all settles the round by sending that beacon in, and a forged one is refused.
   ✅ The coup is dealt by the official Punto Banco rules — the natural, the player's rule and the banker's table — and every cell of those rules is proven by a test.
   ✅ A beacon never expires, so a round settles correctly however late it arrives, unless it was refunded first, after ninety days with no later beacon on record.
4. **You collect, or you do not.**
   ✅ If you won, you claim. If you lost, you do nothing at all.
   ✅ Anyone can send that claim for you, and the money still goes to the account that placed the board.
   📋 The house's helper sends every winner's collection, so you need no KDA to be paid.
   📋 The helper runs on two machines, each with its own budget; if both stopped, a winner could still claim alone.
   🟡 Unclaimed winnings never expire, and nothing sweeps them to the house.

**Why not a Kadena block?** Because whoever produces a Kadena block sees what it would deal
before publishing it, and can throw it away and try again. A beacon produced somewhere else
cannot be thrown away by anyone here.

## What the house can and cannot do

🟡 The contract needs no transaction from the house inside a round and holds no secret of any kind.
✅ Nothing the house holds can change the terms a round already open froze, or its outcome.
✅ The house cannot change what Player or Tie pays, or the rules of the deal.
✅ The house can move the Banker commission for future rounds, and the contract holds it between 2.6932% and 100%.

**Whose key it is.** 📋 The house key is Smart Pacts' own governance keyset: three hardware wallets,
of which **two must approve every single house action** — starting the contract, retuning the
table, taking the earnings out. There is no one-device path to any of them. Those same two
devices are the only ones who can put this contract on the chain at all, and the account the
earnings are paid into can be spent by nobody else either.

**What it can do, said plainly.**
🟡 The house can stop FUTURE rounds: by taking the spare capital out, by raising the minimum bet, or by lowering the share of the pot a round may risk.
✅ Every one of the seven settings stays the house's even after the contract is locked, and every floor and ceiling stays enforced.
✅ There is no ceiling on the minimum bet: the house chose control over a hard bound, so the table can be tuned for the whole life of the contract.
🟡 Every one of those acts is a public transaction on the chain that anyone can see.
✅ A raised minimum binds the next round and never the one already taking bets.

**Locking the contract.**
✅ Locking the contract changes one thing only: it can never be replaced again. Everything else keeps working exactly as it does now.
✅ A locked contract still takes bets, still deals, still pays winners and still refunds.
✅ The pot's capital is not stranded by locking the contract.
✅ Once it is locked, the route that lets the house key take the pot is refused by the contract's own governance, and the pot is untouched.

---

## If the beacon ever stops

✅ A stalled round refunds every stake and takes no fee at all.
✅ A refund opens only after 90 days in which nobody has shown the contract a beacon, and not a second earlier.
✅ A refund also needs evidence on the chain that beacons really stopped, so simply waiting out the clock buys a loser nothing while anyone, the helper included, acts within the ninety days.
✅ One cheap call, which anyone at all can send, shows the contract a newer beacon, and a round locked at or below the newest beacon seen can then never be refunded.
✅ That call settles nothing and moves no money.
✅ Once a later beacon is on the record, a round's refund is closed for good and the round must be settled instead.
✅ That holds at the boundary too: a record exactly equal to the round's own beacon still closes it.

> 🔴 **The honest limits of that arrangement.**
>
> 🟡 If truly nobody acts for 90 days, a player who lost can take their stake back — and because a refund covers a whole round, a winner who never claimed would get their stake back instead of their winnings.
> 🟡 A round can stick for good if its own beacon becomes unreachable after the contract has already seen a later one; that round can be neither settled nor refunded, everything reserved for it stays locked — the players' stakes and the pot's reserve — and because coups are dealt in order every round after it waits with it, while the contract itself keeps taking bets into that queue.
> 📋 The whole of this rests on somebody making that cheap call inside the 90 days.
>
> **If you win, claim it.** ✅ You can always do that alone, from a value anybody can read.

## Who can call what

<!-- promise-gate:caller-legend -->
🟢 anyone · 🔵 the account whose money moves, with its signature · 🔴 the house's key
⚙️ normally reached only through another call of this contract; the house key can reach it
directly, and it then does exactly what that call would do
<!-- /promise-gate:caller-legend -->

### Playing

| | What it takes | What it does |
|---|---|---|
| 🔵 `bet` | Your account and your board: what goes on Player, on Banker and on Tie, and the highest Banker commission you accept | Places one board. ✅ A stake below zero is refused, and so is one finer than the coin allows. ✅ A board whose total is under the minimum is refused. A board that accepts a lower commission than the round's is refused. |
| 🟢 `claim` | A round and the account that placed the board | ✅ Pays a winning board at the commission its round opened with, or a refund from a stalled round. A board can only be claimed once. A board that did not win has nothing to claim. A round that has not settled yet cannot be claimed from. ✅ Nobody can claim a board they never placed. |

- ✅ A board below the table minimum is refused. 🟡 The minimum is a house setting too, 0.01 KDA today, and it can never be set below 0.001 KDA — the floor is roughly twice what it costs the house to pay one winner.
- ✅ A board over the round's limit is refused.
- ✅ A contract-owned account cannot bet: it could never be paid back.
- ✅ A malformed account name cannot bet.

### Ending a round — open to everybody

| | What it takes | What it does |
|---|---|---|
| 🟢 `resolve` | A round and its beacon | Deals the coup and settles the round. ✅ Announces the winner, both hands and the beacon they come from. ✅ Refills the shoe first if it is at the cut, and says so. ✅ Pays the fee out of the pot in the same transaction. A round cannot be settled twice. A beacon for the wrong round does not verify. A re-encoded beacon cannot be used to deal different cards. ✅ A later round is refused until the earlier one is settled. |
| 🟢 `prove-liveness` | Any beacon | ✅ Shows the contract that beacons are still being published; a round locked at or below the newest beacon seen can then never be refunded. ✅ The record of beacons seen cannot be walked backwards. A forged beacon cannot raise it. ✅ Settling an older round does not move it backwards either. |
| 🟢 `void-round` | A stalled round | Opens the refund. Makes each player's whole stake claimable. ✅ A round that has settled can never then be refunded. A refund takes its turn in the shoe's order too. Nothing stays locked once every round is settled. |

### The house's own calls

| | What it takes | What it does |
|---|---|---|
| 🔴 `initialize` | The account the earnings are paid to, and the pot's target size | ✅ Starts the contract, once and once only, with a fresh shoe. ✅ The account must already exist, it cannot be the pot itself, and it cannot be a plain name a stranger could claim first. ✅ An account nobody could ever spend from is refused. |
| 🔴 `set-params` | The table limit, the minimum bet, the pot's target, the betting window, the wait before the beacon, the Banker commission and the cut card | Retunes the table for FUTURE rounds. ✅ Only the house key can retune the table or take money out. ✅ The betting window it sets can never be shorter than 30 seconds or longer than 1 hour. ✅ The share it sets can never be above the whole of the pot's spare capital. ✅ The commission it sets can never go below 2.6932%, and the cut can never go below 14 cards or above a full shoe. |
| 🔴 `withdraw-house` | An amount | Moves spare capital out of the pot to the account named at the start. |

### Putting capital in — open to everybody

| | What it takes | What it does |
|---|---|---|
| 🔵 `fund-house` | An account and an amount | Adds capital to the pot. 🟡 Anyone may strengthen the bank, and doing so grants no claim on it whatsoever. |

### Reading, which costs nothing and needs no key

| | What it takes | What it does |
|---|---|---|
| 🟢 `pot-status` | — | What the pot holds, what it has reserved, the fee right now, the commission, and the largest board on each of Player, Banker and Tie it would accept. ✅ Each maximum it advertises is one a bet actually takes. ✅ It is re-checked mid-round against the pot as it stands. ✅ Nothing is advertised when the only board that would fit is under the minimum. ✅ Beside each maximum it publishes what the pot is sized to keep through a year of play, one 250th of its spare capital, two ninths of that on Tie, and that figure is never what a bet is measured against. |
| 🟢 `shoe-status` | — | The pool as it stands: every kind's count, the cards remaining, the decks, the shoe number, how many coups it has dealt and which round it stands after. |
| 🟢 `get-round` | A round | Everything the round froze when it opened, its winner and both hands. |
| 🟢 `get-board` | A round and an account | That account's board, its stake, and whether it has collected. |
| 🟢 `round-boards` | A round | Every board placed in that round, so whoever is paying the winners can find them. 🟡 It reads and nothing else: it moves no money and writes nothing down. |
| 🟢 `get-params` | — | The table's current settings and the highest beacon the contract has seen. |
| 🟢 `house-account` | — | The pot's account name. ✅ Anyone can work it out, and nobody can take that name under their own key. |
| 🟢 `pot-guard` | — | The lock the pot's account is built from. ✅ Anyone can work the same value out from a transaction alone, so having it hands over nothing. |

### Inside the contract

There is no separate call that opens a round: a board arriving through 🔵 `bet` does. ✅ Opening a round always opens the next round on the terms the game row holds, and nothing can be passed in: a board carries three stakes and the commission it accepts, and the contract refuses a board carrying anything else before a line of its own code runs.

### Plumbing — the contract's building blocks

Everything on a public blockchain is public, so these can all be *called* by anyone — but they
exist for the contract's own use. Each one answers a question, works something out without
writing it down, or refuses a bad input. **None of them can move money or write a record.** They
are listed so this page accounts for every function in the contract, with nothing invisible.

| | What it is for |
|---|---|
| `coup-from-cards` · `banker-draws` · `finish` | The rules of Punto Banco, written out: the natural on 8 or 9, the player's rule, the banker's table against the player's third card, and the winner by the final totals. |
| `card-value` · `hand-total` | A card's value — an ace is one, tens and pictures are nothing — and a hand's total, modulo ten. |
| `draw-cards` · `draw` · `kind-at` · `adjust` · `restore` | How cards are picked from the pool by the beacon, one at a time, and how the unused ones go back. |
| `board-vector` · `board-payout` · `pay-punto` · `pay-banco` · `pay-tie` · `slot` | What a board is owed on each of the three outcomes, and on the one that happened. |
| `validate-wager` · `enforce-prec` | Checks every stake on a board and adds up the total; refuses a number finer than the coin allows. |
| `fee-scale` · `fee-for` · `banco-edge` | The fee the pot is charging right now, from how full the pot is and each bet's own edge — the Banker's from the commission in force. |
| `box-max` | The round's limit, its accrued fee, what each slot already owes, a box's payout per unit on each slot, and the fee per unit | The largest stake on that box the limit still admits: the smallest of the three slot bounds, floored to the coin's precision. Never above what a bet takes, within two units of the last decimal on Banker and one on Player and Tie, on every box. |
| `vmax` | The largest number in a list — how the worst outcome is found. |
| `curr-time` | The chain's own clock. It is the previous block's time. |
| `rkey` · `bkey` | How the contract builds its record keys — rounds · boards. |

## What is not built, or not true today

- ⛔ **A locked contract.**
- ⛔ **The play page for this table.**

## True of the whole thing

1. ✅ **The table depends on one other contract, the beacon verifier, pinned to its exact code**:
   against any other code, this contract refuses to load at all.
   ✅ That verifier can never be replaced, so the dependency cannot change underneath a locked table.
   🟡 It holds no money, keeps no records and has no key of its own.
2. The shoe is 8 decks of 52: 416 cards of 52 kinds, and a coup draws at most 6 of them.
   Every card's value is the official one, and the whole shoe's values add up as 8 decks must.
   The rules of the deal agree with the official Punto Banco tableau in every cell: all 100 opening totals, all 80 banker decisions against a player's third card, and all 16 cases where the player stands.
3. The table's chain is **chain 2**: the chain where the earnings account already holds its
   balance, and where Smart Pacts' other live contracts already run.
   📋 **The contract runs on a chain that carried none of its records when it started.**
   📋 **The account the earnings are paid to exists and is spendable** — the contract refused to
   start until it could be paid, but it cannot tell whose an account is.
4. ✅ Gas is small: a bet, a deal and a collection each cost a small fraction of what one block allows.
   🟡 A bet is never sponsored — a player funds their own stake, always.
5. ✅ The books balance after every kind of settlement, checked independently of the contract's own
   bookkeeping, and the shoe's count of cards agrees with its pool after every coup.
6. The house's upgrade authority, `GOVERNANCE`, backs nothing else at all, which is
   why locking the contract changes only whether it can be replaced. Its day-to-day authority,
   `ADMIN`, is a separate permission and keeps working afterwards.
